source.author: verg
source.text: Urbis uti captae casum convolsaque vidit limina tectorum et medium in penetralibus hostem, arma diu senior desueta trementibus aevo circumdat nequiquam umeris, et inutile ferrum cingitur, ac densos fertur moriturus in hostis.
source.text_original: Urbis uti captae casum convolsaque vidit / limina tectorum et medium in penetralibus hostem, / arma diu senior desueta trementibus aevo / circumdat nequiquam umeris, et inutile ferrum / cingitur, ac densos fertur moriturus in hostis.
source.text_english: When he saw the fall of the captured city and the doorposts of the houses torn down and the enemy in the very heart of the inner shrines, long unused in age he vainly girds on his shaking shoulders his weapons, and cinches on useless steel, and, about to die, he is borne against the dense ranks of the enemy.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quam multa leo cunctatus in arta mole virum rictuque genas et lumina pressit, sic curae subiere ducem, ferrumne capessat imbelle atque aevi senior gestamina primi an patres regnique acuat mutabile vulgus.
reuse.text_original: quam multa leo cunctatus in arta / mole virum rictuque genas et lumina pressit, / sic curae subiere ducem, ferrumne capessat / imbelle atque aevi senior gestamina primi / an patres regnique acuat mutabile vulgus.
reuse.text_english: How long the lion, after delaying in the cramped mass, pressed the man’s cheeks and eyes with its jaws; so cares came over the leader, whether he should seize the sword, though unfit for war and now older than the burdens of his first age, or whether he should rouse the fathers and the changeable common people of the kingdom.
